key_insight: Introduce a 4D (space + time) latent reward computed in feature/latent space to steer pretrained video diffusion models toward geometrically/world-consistent outputs, without modifying model architectures or repeatedly decoding to RGB.
problem_solved: Video diffusion models often produce temporally or geometrically inconsistent frames; prior fixes add modules or use costly RGB-space alignment limited to static scenes. This paper enables efficient, geometry-aware consistency for dynamic video generation while preserving pretrained model generalization.
method: Compute a 4D latent reward that measures spatial and temporal consistency in latent/feature space (avoiding repeated VAE → RGB decoding).
Use the latent reward to guide the diffusion sampling/optimization process (reward-guided policy/optimization) so outputs align with world-consistent priors across time.
Keep the original generator unchanged (plug-and-play with internet-scale pretrained video diffusion models), enabling applicability to dynamic scenes and efficient inference.
impact: Provides a practical, generalizable way to improve geometric and temporal coherence in video generation without retraining or architectural hacks—useful for high-fidelity video editing, simulation, and downstream perception tasks.

paper_title: VGGRPO: Towards World-Consistent Video Generation with 4D Latent Reward
paper_authors: Zhaochong An, Orest Kupyn, Théo Uscidda, Andrea Colaco, Karan Ahuja
